stories.headline: Pavel-Babiš clash over NATO Ankara summit delegation escalates into constitutional confrontation
stories.summary: President Pavel and PM Babiš failed to agree on the composition of the Czech delegation for the July NATO summit in Ankara, with Pavel threatening a constitutional (competence) complaint if blocked from attending. The dispute sharpened around a Friday Prague Castle meeting at which Babiš arrived 15 minutes late, triggering a secondary public row over protocol and the limits of presidential authority, with extensive commentary from opposition, analysts, and former officials including ex-President Klaus.

stories.headline: SPD and coalition drive parliament to oppose Sudeten German congress in Brno, drawing AfD contradictions
stories.summary: Speaker Tomio Okamura convened an extraordinary parliamentary session to pass a resolution opposing the upcoming Sudeten German Regional Association congress in Brno, pushing a nationalist agenda that drew criticism from analysts and opponents who noted SPD's simultaneous close ties to Germany's AfD, which itself has not consistently opposed the Beneš decrees. The debate produced heated late-night scenes in the chamber, with the SPD floor leader shouting profanities at the opposition.

stories.headline: Thousands protest Prague media reform plans; EBU warns legislation threatens public broadcaster independence
stories.summary: Thousands of Czechs filled Prague's Old Town Square on 5 May to protest Babiš government plans to overhaul funding of Czech Television and Czech Radio, with critics warning reforms amount to capture of public media. The European Broadcasting Union wrote to the prime minister warning the draft legislation could undermine financial stability and independence; analysts described the moves as a 'soft capture' strategy.

stories.headline: Czech National Bank holds rates at 3.5%, signals possible hike as inflation risks turn pro-inflationary
stories.summary: The CNB board voted unanimously to hold the benchmark rate at 3.5% at its May meeting, but Governor Aleš Michl shifted the balance-of-risks assessment to pro-inflationary and said the bank's forecast now foresees one to two rate hikes later in 2026. The CNB also worsened its economic outlook and flagged April CPI of 2.5%—above the 2% target for the first time this year.

stories.headline: ANO retains large polling lead but slips two points in May surveys as STAN holds second place
stories.summary: Multiple April/May opinion polls show ANO winning a hypothetical election with roughly 32% of the vote—down about two points from March—while STAN holds second place and SPD improves slightly. New Kantar polling also explored what would happen without the SPOLU coalition, finding only ODS would pass the threshold alone.

stories.headline: Nagyová convicted in Stork Nest subsidy fraud; Agrofert EU subsidy freeze questioned
stories.summary: A Czech court convicted Jana Nagyová (ANO MEP, Babiš's former partner) of EU subsidy fraud in the Stork Nest case, sentencing her to a three-year suspended term and a fine. Babiš himself was dropped from the case after parliament shielded him by rejecting his prosecution. Separately, questions emerged about whether Czech agricultural authorities had prematurely unfrozen EU subsidies to Agrofert after assuring Brussels they were blocked.

stories.summary: Finnish defence company Patria signed memoranda of understanding with three Czech state enterprises—Vojenský technický ústav, VOP CZ, and Vojenský výzkumný ústav—positioning the Patria AMV XP 8×8 CZ as a candidate to replace Pandur II vehicles in the Czech Armed Forces, with high localisation and lifecycle maintenance promised.

stories.headline: Czech Republic marks 81st Victory Day with Vítkov ceremony; Pavel warns against resignation to force
stories.summary: President Pavel, PM Babiš, and senior officials attended the official Victory Day commemoration at Vítkov on 8–9 May. Pavel used the ceremony to warn that security and freedom are again under threat and must be actively defended. The ceremony was overshadowed by the ongoing Pavel-Babiš dispute that erupted the same morning. A separate Freedom Festival in Pilsen with some 300 historical WWII vehicles also drew attention.

stories.headline: Babiš announces appointment of former NATO ambassador Landovský as government envoy for alliance commitments
stories.summary: PM Babiš announced the cabinet will formally appoint Jakub Landovský, former Czech ambassador to NATO, as government envoy for fulfilling Czech commitments to the alliance, including the 2% GDP defence spending target. Critics in the opposition dismissed the new post as a sinecure, while Babiš insisted Landovský would serve without additional pay.

stories.headline: Czech public mostly backs maintaining or increasing defence spending but reluctant to serve personally
stories.summary: Two surveys published this week showed that only around 17% of Czechs favour cutting defence spending while majorities support maintaining or exceeding current NATO levels. A separate Median poll found 91% consider themselves patriots but over half believe defence is primarily a matter for professional soldiers, not citizens.

stories.headline: President Pavel promotes ten new generals including BIS deputy director
stories.summary: President Pavel appointed ten new brigadier generals at Prague Castle, including Antonín Genser as BIS (domestic intelligence) deputy director, special forces commander Tomáš Krampl, and NCOZ (organised crime centre) director Jiří Mazánek. The appointment of one general drew protest from the Confederation of Political Prisoners over his past service in the Communist-era secret police.
